subject: SLO acceptance criteria, GPU-fit notes & proposed pilot milestones
messages:
From: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwoodinference.com>
To: Alex Morgan <alex.morgan@cobalthealth.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>, Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Mon, 20 Feb 2028 15:12:00 -0800
Subject: Post-demo recap & next steps — SLOs / pilot sizing

Hi Alex — thanks again for carving out time today. Quick recap from our call and a proposal for next steps so we have clear acceptance criteria for the pilot: 

Key points I captured:
- Target 95th percentile latency: 120 ms for short-chat flows (<= 256 tokens).
- Sustained throughput target: 800 qps aggregated across 10 logical shards (expected burst to 1.6k qps).
- Concurrency per model instance: expected 20–40 concurrent requests; streaming required for token-by-token responses in agent workflows.
- Data controls: traffic from these endpoints must stay within your VPC during the pilot (private deployment).

Open questions we flagged:
1) Typical request size distribution — you mentioned most requests are ~40 tokens but some batch analytics jobs reach 1k tokens. Can you confirm percentile breakdown?
2) Are there multiple independent model classes (summary vs. clinical Q&A) that we should route to different GPU types?
3) Any org constraints on GPU family (e.g., NVIDIA A10 vs H100) driven by procurement?

Proposed next steps (attached: pilot_sla_matrix.xlsx with our baseline measurements and candidate GPU profiles):
- You: confirm token distribution and the three representative prompt sets by EOD Thu (22 Feb).
- Us: run focused KV-cache and streaming microbenchmarks against the supplied prompt sets and return a short matrix with latency/throughput projections for A10 / A100 / H100 by Tue 27 Feb. (we'll attach the raw bench PDF)
- Joint: align on acceptance criteria for go/no-go after pilot (pass if 95p latency <120ms and sustained 800 qps with <3% error rate).

If that all looks right I’ll kick this off with engineering and loop in Soojin for streaming/kv-cache tuning.

Best,
Naomi
Director, Solutions — Redwood Inference
naomi.feldman@redwoodinference.com
+1 (415) 555-0198

Attachments: pilot_sla_matrix.xlsx (spreadsheet), kv-cache-bench.pdf (report)
From: Alex Morgan <alex.morgan@cobalthealth.com>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, 21 Feb 2028 10:34:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Post-demo recap & next steps — SLOs / pilot sizing

Thanks Naomi — this is great and captures the call well. A few clarifications from our side: 

- Token distribution: roughly 70% of calls are 20–60 tokens, 25% are 200–600 (analytics/summary), and ~5% exceed 800 tokens. We'll provide a CSV with sample prompts by Thursday.
- Model classes: yes — two primary classes: "clinical-qna" (latency-sensitive, streaming) and "batch-summary" (throughput-oriented, higher token counts).
- Procurement: we prefer to target A100 or H100 for the pilot; A10 is likely acceptable if the economics are favorable, but we will need procurement sign-off for H100.

One additional constraint: any pilot instances must support our logging mask rules (PII redaction) and token-level audit logs retained for 30 days. If you can confirm that's supported in the private deployment, we can proceed.

I'll attach the sample prompt CSV in a follow-up.

—Alex
Alex Morgan
Head of Platform — Cobalt Health
alex.morgan@cobalthealth.com
From: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwoodinference.com>
To: Alex Morgan <alex.morgan@cobalthealth.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>, Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Wed, 22 Feb 2028 08:02:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Post-demo recap & next steps — SLOs / pilot sizing

Appreciate the quick turnaround, Alex — that's exactly what we needed. Two quick confirmations: 

- Private deployment: yes — token-level audit logs and PII redaction hooks (we provide a pre-filter + post-filter plugin model) are supported. We will ship a small schema for the masking rules for your security team to vet.
- Pilot hardware plan: we'll run the bench matrix on A100 (40GB), H100 (80GB), and A10 (24GB) to show tradeoffs. Our bench will include: steady-state qps, 95/99p latency with streaming enabled, and cold-start KV-cache hit/miss scenarios.

Action: Ben and Priyom will start the bench with your sample prompts as soon as they arrive. Expected deliverable: combined bench PDF + an updated pilot_sla_matrix.xlsx by EOD Mon 27 Feb. 

Ben / Priyom — can you validate the proposed acceptance criteria below and confirm the staffing estimate for the pilot run? We expect ~3 engineering-days of focused bench time plus a small Ops window to provision private nodes.

Acceptance criteria (proposal):
- 95p latency for clinical-qna streaming flows <= 120 ms
- Sustained throughput for batch-summary >= 800 qps (aggregated) with <3% request error rate
- Concurrency: per-instance tail latency remains within 1.8x median at 40 concurrent streams
- KV-cache: warm cache reduces token compute by >= 40% in repeat workflows

Thanks — will stand up the bench infra after we get the CSV.

Naomi
From: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwoodinference.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>, Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwoodinference.com>, Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Wed, 22 Feb 2028 09:05:00 -0800
Subject: INTERNAL: Pilot run scheduling & quick technical asks (no external recipients)

Ben/Priyom/Soojin — moving this internal thread here for planning. Alex sent sample prompts (incoming CSV) and confirmed H100/A100 preference.

Immediate asks:
1) Priyom: please draft a short bench plan (1 page) showing microbench stages: small-chat streaming, mid-length summaries, long-batch. Include exact parameters we will run (qps targets, concurrency, sequence lengths, batch sizes).
2) Ben: inventory of private cloud node images and any infra work required to stand up H100 nodes in Cobalt's VPC; estimate time to provision (hours).
3) Soojin: streaming KV-cache tuning — we should test two cache stratagems (prefix cache + ephemeral request cache) and measure token reduction impact. Also validate that our masking plugin doesn't add >10ms per request on median.

Staffing estimate: 3 eng-days + 4 ops-hours (provisioning) — is that feasible? If not, call out the delta.

I'll schedule a 30-min internal sync tomorrow 9am PT to align before we run benches.

Thanks,
Naomi
